subject: How does STAN define priors on covariance matrices?

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: How does STAN define priors on covariance matrices?
parts:
How does STAN define priors on covariance matrices when no explicit priors are hard coded by the user?

 I'm a writing up the methods section for a paper at the moment, and realized I did not know exactly what was going on "under the hood" when it came to the prior on the VCOV matrix for the random effects in my hierarchical model.

 I'm using the cholesky decompose as defined in the user manual:

              LW <- cholesky_decompose(SigmaBetaW);

                  BetaW[j] <- MuBetaW + LW * ABetaW[j]; 

I simply declare SigmaBetaW as a VCOV matrix in the parameters block. I do not specify any particular prior.

Does STAN utilize the scaled LKJ correlation matrix as a prior 'under the hood'? If so what is the specification?

Thanks for the help!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How does STAN define priors on covariance matrices?
parts:
Any variable declared in Stan without a prior is given
a uniform prior on its support. For covariance matrices,
that's an improper prior.

The unconstrained parameterization is a Cholesky factor with
log-transformed diagonal. The Jacobian adjustment
to make it uniform on covariance (symmetric, positive-definite
in Stan) matrices is described in the manual near the end in the
variable transform chapter.

We'd love to hear about any publications with models fit
using Stan.

- Bob
